body:
`SeaIceMomentumEquation` defaults to `ocean_surface_height = ZeroField()`, which is an integer `ZeroField`. `extended_surface_height` passes it through unchanged, so the free-surface tilt in the momentum kernels is an `Int` while the other terms are floats, and the tendency becomes a `Union{Float64, Int64}` (in `conditional_δy_f` via `∂yᶜᶠᶜ`). On Julia 1.13 / LLVM 20 this crashes the NVPTX backend while compiling the kernel (segfault in libnvptx `tryLDG`; `llc` reports `Cannot select: AtomicLoad`).

This PR:
- converts an integer `ZeroField` to `ZeroField(eltype(grid))` in `extended_surface_height`;
- adds a no-op `refresh_and_fill_external_field!(::ZeroField, ::ZeroField)`, since the converted `η` is no longer `===` the user's `η₀` and is refreshed every step;
- tests that the default `η` has the grid's float type (Float32 and Float64) and that a time step with it leaves `u` at zero.

Tested with `TEST_GROUP=timestepping` on CPU. On a GH200, a sea-ice run that crashed at kernel compilation on Julia 1.13 runs with this change and matches the unfixed Julia 1.12 run in Σhℵ.

title: Give the default ocean surface height the grid's float type
